newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Japanese emperor ends 10-day trip to Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Japanese emperor ends 10-day trip to Brazil.

text.p: Japan's Emperor Akihito and Empress Michiko ended a 10-day trip to Brazil on Monday with a visit to a Rio de Janeiro community centre which runs educational programmes for needy children from shantytowns.
They arrived at the centre to a warm welcome by Rio's Mayor Luiz Paulo Conde and crowds of cheering children holding red and white balloons and waving Japanese flags.
Akihito and Michiko were shown around the facilities before watching some of the children perform Capoeira, an Afro-Brazilian dance derived from a foot fighting technique imported by Angolan slaves.

The couple then sped off to Rio's Galeao air force base amid tight security to board a flight to Buenos Aires, the last stop on the first Japanese imperial visit to Latin America. They will spend three days in the Argentine capital before returning home.

The couple arrived in Rio de Janeiro on Sunday and met with state Governor Marcelo Alencar after visiting the city's botanical garden, meeting with members of Rio's Japanese community and attending a samba dance exhibition.

Akihito and Michiko began their visit to Brazil May 31 with a trip to the Amazon at Belem port where the river flows into the Atlantic, then dined with President Fernando Henrique Cardoso in Brasilia.

They spent two days in industrial Sao Paulo, home to most of the 1.3 million Brazilians of Japanese descent, before travelling to Parana's state capital of Curitiba, where Brazil's second largest Japanese colony lives.
Despite tight security, the couple thrilled fans in both cities and was greeted by the traditional Japanese patriotic cry of "Banzai!"
Brazil is home to the largest Japanese community outside of Japan.
